A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EfficientQAT work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original quantization and instruction-tuning results, component ablations, efficiency measurements, and multimodal experiments in Appendix G.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds a weights-only ablation and comparisons with matched calibration-sample counts.

M1.justification: Both versions use Block-AP to train weights, scales, and zero points blockwise, followed by E2E-QP with fixed quantized weights and trainable scales by default. The quantization equations and training procedures remain unchanged; the new weights-only experiment is an ablation.

E1.justification: Both retain RedPajama, WikiText2/C4, the same five commonsense tasks, Alpaca/MMLU, and the four multimodal benchmarks used with LLaVA. The new calibration-budget comparisons reuse existing datasets and tasks. Removing 4-bit configurations changes settings and results, not task coverage.

E2.justification: The quality-comparison set is substantially revised. v3 removes LLM-QAT and PB-LLM quality results, adds CBQ perplexity results, and adds OmniQuant comparisons for Llama-3. Perplexity comparisons also lose 3-bit QuIP#, AQLM 1x16, and 2-bit group-64 OmniQuant. BitDistiller and DB-LLM results are partly consolidated from v2 Table 2. AQLM 1x16 accuracy remains in Table 17, and the training-time comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Base-model quality evaluation narrows from 2/3/4-bit to 2/3-bit, while instruction-tuning retains 4-bit settings. Appendix H adds comparisons matching 64, 128, 256, and 512 calibration samples, and Section 4.1 introduces relative gain as an additional metric. DB-LLM's Llama-3-8B group size is reported as 128 in v2 Table 2 and 64 in v3 Tables 1–2; this does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds a weights-only control to the Block-AP parameter ablation and tests whether advantages over GPTQ/OmniQuant persist with equal calibration-sample counts. It also analyzes relative error recovery across model sizes. Existing component, sample-count, group-size, and calibration-dataset analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The added sample-count experiments concern calibration data, not repeated runs.

E6.justification: v3 removes the 4-bit base-model accuracy and perplexity results, including the detailed appendix table, and adds results for the new controls and revised comparator set. At the retained Llama-3-70B 3-bit group-128 setting, reported accuracy changes from 72.42 to 73.96, moving above AWQ's unchanged 73.65; WikiText2/C4 perplexity changes from 4.19/7.43 to 4.21/7.46. DB-LLM's Llama-2-7B group-64 accuracy changes from 55.12 to 56.93. Instruction-tuning and multimodal results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 newly defines relative gain as (EfficientQAT accuracy - DB-LLM accuracy)/(FP16 accuracy - DB-LLM accuracy). This is a limited mathematical-definition addition. Quantization equations, Appendix B gradients, and the model-size formula remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same two-stage novelty, applicability, performance, and efficiency claims, including 2-bit Llama-2-70B training in 41 hours. The introductory sentence claiming parity with vector quantization is deleted, but equivalent wording remains in Figure 1's caption.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations involving PTQ scaling laws, preservation of pretrained knowledge through joint parameter optimization, and deployment/generalization tradeoffs with vector quantization. New Section 6 explicitly discusses the remaining FP16 performance gap and dependence on diverse training data, including possible limitations in data-scarce or specialized domains.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 clarifies that full-precision weights mean Float16 or BFloat16. Appendix H newly states baseline calibration budgets of 128 samples for GPTQ/OmniQuant and 20k for DB-LLM. Conversely, Section 4.1 omits the previously explicit 4-bit E2E-QP learning rate. Code access, hardware disclosures, and most implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds PrefixQuant, Kumar et al.'s precision scaling laws, and Ouyang et al.'s quantization scaling study. These support additional positioning around weight-activation quantization and scaling behavior. The existing related-work discussion and earlier cited works are largely retained.

P1.justification: Section 4.1 is reorganized from separate PTQ/QAT discussions into accuracy, perplexity, and scaling discussions. v3 adds a limitations section, acknowledgements, and Appendix H, moving Full Results to Appendix I. Most methodological prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 changes the main text and references to two columns and substantially rearranges displays. Figure 1 moves to the first page, replaces its vector-comparison curves with a revised uniform-method comparison, and loses its timing panel; timing results remain in Table 9. Main result tables are consolidated and simplified. The old 4-bit Table 15 is replaced by a calibration-budget table, while former Figure 4 becomes Table 8 with unchanged results.

improvement.justification: The weights-only ablation, equal-sample controls, and explicit limitations strengthen validation and qualification. However, removing 4-bit results and competitive perplexity baselines reduces completeness. New reporting inconsistencies also weaken reliability: Appendix H states 8.02 where Table 15 reports 8.95, and Section 4.4 drops the AQLM single-GPU exception still shown in Table 9. These competing benefits and harms prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
